value.body: The Shipping Corporation of India (SCI) is a central public-sector company under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways that owns and operates Indian-flagged ships — tankers, bulk carriers and other vessels. It employs deck and engine officers, ratings and cadets for its fleet.

items.label: Ownership
items.note: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

items.label: Licence needed
items.note: For officer ranks, matched to the rank

items.label: Ships owned by SCI
items.note: 54 in overseas trade, 9 in coastal trade
items.source: Indian Shipping Statistics 2024, M/o Ports, Shipping & Waterways (D.G. Shipping data)

items.label: Oil tankers in SCI fleet
items.note: Includes acid, gas and LPG carriers; dry bulk carriers are the next largest group (14)
items.source: Indian Shipping Statistics 2024, M/o Ports, Shipping & Waterways

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Officer posts need the DG Shipping Certificate of Competency (CoC) for the rank, valid STCW courses, a medical certificate and a CDC. SCI advertises sea-staff and cadet openings on its website; selection is by application, interview and document checks.

value.title: At a glance
items: Terms (permanent or contract) depend on the specific notice.
Pay, contract length and leave differ from private and foreign-flag companies, so comparing the actual offer terms is part of the decision.
Openings depend on the size of SCI's fleet, which changes as ships are bought and sold.

value.title: Ships owned by SCI
value.note: Owned fleet only, coastal plus overseas; chartered ships are not included. Fleet size says little directly about hiring, which also depends on crewing contracts.
value.source: Indian Shipping Statistics 2024 (Table 4.1), M/o Ports, Shipping & Waterways
